_comment: This is the model's final answer, and it is guilty by construction: the
flow asserts the reply contains 'sunny', and this reply says the opposite.
A flow asserting on it must FAIL.
Why this needs proving at all: every end-to-end use of `assert: reply
contains` in the suite asserts text the model was always going to produce,
so those flows pass whether the assertion works or not. Replace the
assertion with an unconditional PASS and nothing would notice.
The 0.9.0 record makes the stakes concrete. A streaming client handed one
buffered body assembles identical text, so this exact assertion stayed
green for precisely the defect it existed to catch. An assertion whose
failing direction is never exercised is where that class of bug hides.
Do not 'fix' this reply to contain the asserted word. It is evidence, and
it is supposed to disappoint the assertion.

message.content: It is overcast and raining heavily in Nairobi.
